Envy can arise when another person or group has something you want or need and do not have.

## Words describing envy

Bitterness, covetousness, craving, discontent, disgruntlement, displeasure, dissatisfaction, feeling downhearted, greed, feeling green-eyed, longing, pettiness, resentment, and wishfulness.

## Prompting events and interpretations

Events include another person having what you want, receiving recognition, seeming more successful, or being included while you are not. Interpretations can include believing you deserve what they have, the difference is unfair, you are inferior or unlucky, or you are unappreciated.

## Body changes, expressions, and action urges

Muscles, teeth, jaw, or mouth may tighten; the face may feel hot and the body rigid. Urges and actions include competing, taking or spoiling what another has, criticizing, gossiping, comparing, withdrawing, or trying to improve your own situation.

## Aftereffects

Attention can narrow to what others have, while your own life is discounted. Resentment, comparison, and resolutions to change may persist.

## When envy fits the facts

Envy fits when another person or group has something you want or need and do not have.

## Acting on the urge, Opposite Action, and Checking the Facts

When effective, use envy as information about a goal and take steps to improve your own situation. When acting on it would be ineffective, do not damage what others have, count what is present in your life without discounting it, check the other person's full situation, and relax the body.
